trust_decision.summary: A server-owned configuration file (any format the panel selected) must be size-bounded before wings buffers it for template replacement: ConfigurationFile.Parse refuses files over 64 MB via file.Stat() before any rewrite, and each of the six format readers reads through a 64 MB io.LimitReader.

landing_point.why: The summary says parsed config files can OOM wings; the only parse entry and its format switch sit here, directly above the whole-file io.ReadAll / ini.Load / etree.ReadFrom / bufio.Scanner calls, so an engineer looks at Parse and the reader they can reproduce with first.

fix_sites.entry_point: ConfigurationFile.Parse (public API) <- Server.UpdateConfigurationFiles (server/config_parser.go:39) <- POST /api/servers/:server/power (router/router_server.go:92), websocket SetStateEvent start (router/websocket/websocket.go:376), POST /api/servers install-with-auto-start (router/router_system.go:102); also wings CLI boot restore (cmd/root.go:239) and crash auto-restart (server/crash.go:90)
shared constant used by all six format readers
ConfigurationFile.Parse -> parseYamlFile (io.ReadAll, also covers the yml alias)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: config.FromFile reads the daemon's own YAML at config.DefaultLocation with os.ReadFile and no cap, but that file is operator-owned, mode 0600, and only read at daemon startup or by `wings diagnostics` (cmd/root.go:404, cmd/diagnostics.go:112) - never from a server's data directory - so a solver can argue it is outside 'maliciously created parsed config files' for servers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An oversized config file must stay byte-for-byte intact and must not block the server from booting: the fix returns before any Truncate and the caller only logs the error. A LimitReader-only fix instead truncates and rewrites the file with just the first 64 MB, silently destroying user data.

O6_input_shapes: six parser format values supplied by the panel: json, yaml/yml, ini, xml, properties, file (parser/parser.go:223-236)
whole-file read vs line-by-line buffering: io.ReadAll (json, yaml, properties), ini.Load, etree ReadFrom, bufio.Scanner with maxTextScanTokenSize (parser/parser.go:402, 429, 544, 322, 243, 479-480)
file opened read-write via ufs Touch, so Stat describes a file the parser will later truncate and rewrite (server/config_parser.go:32; parser/parser.go:505-513)
missing file: only the `file` parser is skipped when absent (server/config_parser.go:25-30); the other formats are still opened/created at server/config_parser.go:32

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Daemon config reload/read path: config.FromFile buffers the whole YAML config into memory with os.ReadFile before yaml.Unmarshal, no size cap
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: operator-owned 0600 file at a fixed path, read only at startup or by the diagnostics command, not a server-owned config parsed at server start

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a seventh format reader (e.g. toml/env/csv) added to the Parse switch that buffers the whole file with a new library and forgets the cap
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the switch already carries six formats and the cap is a separate call inside each reader rather than at the dispatch

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a caller-side size/existence pre-check next to the existing `f.Parser == parser.File` stat
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the pinned commit 3317ce1 just edited this exact spot to skip missing files, so a maintainer adding a size check here is the natural next step

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another server-owned file read whole (e.g. a .gitignore/ignore-list variant or a config preview helper) reusing the hand-rolled 32 KiB cap shape
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the repo already hand-writes per-file size caps for this exact 'read a small server-owned file' job, and a copy that forgets the check is easy to write

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same 64 MB cap applied to the daemon config loader
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is the second config-file parser in the tree and shares the identical os.ReadFile-then-parse shape

O9_family: uncontrolled resource consumption / unbounded memory allocation (CWE-400, CWE-770, CWE-789)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.24.0 (go.mod:3), Makefile and Dockerfile present, no vendor/ so modules are fetched at build time
O10_build.project_tests: no tests in parser/ at the pinned commit; adjacent area tests are internal/ufs/fs_unix_test.go and server/filesystem/filesystem_test.go; the fix diff adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Put a 64 MB size check next to the existing existence stat in server/config_parser.go:26 (which only runs for parser.File) instead of in ConfigurationFile.Parse and in each of the six format readers.

out_of_scope_notes: Panel/remote responses are read whole elsewhere (remote/http.go:236, cmd/configure.go:141-147); unrelated to this advisory's config-file parsing, not pursued.
server/backup.go:46-50 already caps the .pteroignore read at 32 KiB - noted only as an existing in-repo precedent, not as a route.
unverified: repo source size in MB (no shell available to measure), so neither tiny_repo nor giant_repo is flagged
whether a later release caps config.FromFile (the input gives no latest release/commit to check)
the exact test harness for the parser: no parser tests exist at the pinned commit, so how the fix would be scored behaviourally is unverified

a defence does exist at the pinned commit - maxTextScanTokenSize = 64 MB (parser/parser.go:34-35, 480) - but it only bounds a single scanner token; the accumulated bytes.Buffer still grows with the whole file, so it did not stop the OOM
